location.name: Torres del Paine National Park
location.tagline: Granite towers, blue icebergs and pumas at the bottom of the world.
location.intro: Torres del Paine is Chile's showpiece of Patagonia: three sheer granite towers, the jagged Cuernos del Paine, and turquoise lakes fed by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Guanacos graze the steppe while condors ride the wind overhead, and trekkers come from everywhere to walk the famous W route.
facts: "Paine" means "blue" in the language of the Tehuelche (Aonikenk) people, fitting for a park full of glacier-blue lakes.
The lakes get their unreal colors mostly from rock flour, fine sediment ground up by glaciers and suspended in the water.
In 2014, scientists found fossils of at least 46 ichthyosaurs, dolphin-like marine reptiles, after retreating glacier ice exposed new rock in the park.
Grey Glacier, the park's largest at about 15 km long, is split into two arms by an island of rock in the middle of the ice.
Three big wildfires, in 1985, 2005 and 2011-12, were all blamed on visitors and together burned roughly 480 square kilometers of the park.
location.bestTime: November to March, the southern summer, when days are long and the trails and refugios are open (expect wind any month).
location.gettingThere: Fly JFK to Santiago (nonstop overnight), connect to Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales, then it's about 112 km by road from Puerto Natales to the park.
location.tip: Book refugios or campsites before you go; you need reservations for overnight stays on the W and O treks, and they sell out months ahead.
